insights.claim: Data Connect Hub implements a two-tier authentication architecture: kube-rbac-proxy sidecar handles Kubernetes TokenReview for external authentication, while the REST service's actix-web middleware enforces tenant isolation via a required X-Tenant-ID header.
insights.reasoning: The controller deploys kube-rbac-proxy as a sidecar (line 355: setDeploymentImage for kube-rbac-proxy) and configures token review audiences (line 362-367). The REST service validate_headers middleware independently requires X-Tenant-ID (middleware.rs:20-43) and extracts Authorization headers (middleware.rs:45-49). This layered approach separates platform-level identity verification from application-level tenant scoping.

insights.claim: The Rust services select aws_lc_rs as the rustls crypto provider but do not enable the fips feature, leaving FIPS compliance status unverified despite using a FIPS-capable provider.
insights.reasoning: Cargo.toml line 78 specifies rustls with features=["aws_lc_rs"] and default-features=false. The aws-lc-rs crate supports FIPS validation when built with the fips feature and a FIPS-validated aws-lc library, but neither is configured. The ring crate (a non-FIPS provider) remains as a transitive dependency. This means the component uses a FIPS-capable stack but does not activate FIPS mode.

insights.claim: The operator's controller-to-service communication pattern uses in-cluster HTTP clients (NewHTTPConnectionTypeClient, NewHTTPMigrationClient) for synchronizing connection types and migrations between the Go controller and the deployed Rust REST service.
insights.reasoning: Three reconcilers (InitDataConnectionTypeReconciler at line 214, ConfigMapWatcherReconciler at line 230, SecretWatcherReconciler at line 239) create HTTP clients via RestServiceURLResolver to communicate with the deployed REST service. This cross-language (Go-to-Rust) controller-to-service integration pattern is unusual and creates a runtime dependency of the operator on its own managed workloads.
